findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

The operator’s Certified Food Protection Manager certificate is not present. Ensure that there is always a person in charge who is a certified food protection manager.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw beef stored above cooked tortillas in the prep cooler. The PIC was informed and the item was moved to the bottom. Ensure raw meats are never stored above ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no stem thermometer available during inspection. Ensure a stem thermometer is available at all times of food prep. A follow-up will be conducted at the next event to ensure a thermometer is present and in use.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no test strips available on the truck. The PIC was informed and strips were acquired. Ensure test strips are available at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The prep cooler in the food truck is still not operational and an ice bath is being utilized to keep items cold held. The equipment either needs to be repaired or replaced in the truck to ensure that food can be properly cold held at 41F or under. A follow up is scheduled for 4/15/2025 to ensure that the prep table has either been repaired and is functioning properly or has been replaced and the TCS items are being properly cold held.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The facility brought Chlorine test strips instead of Quaternary ammonium test strips for their Quaternary ammonium spray bottle sanitizer. Ensure QUATERNARY AMMONIUM test strips are available at all times on the truck to be able to test the concentration of the sanitizer. A follow up is scheduled for 4/15/2025 to ensure that these test strips are available on the food truck.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The operator’s Certified Food Protection Manager certificate expired in January and no one else has their certificate. Ensure that there is always a person in charge who is a certified food protection manager.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There was a trash can in front of the handwashing sink and a necklace inside of it. CORRECTED- The trash can was moved from being in front of it and the necklace was removed. It was also discovered that the handwashing sink did not have any power to it to provide running water. The operator brought a bucket of potable water with spout to create a temporary handwashing sink. The handwashing sink was supplied with paper towels and hand soap. Ensure that handwashing sins are maintained to be accessible at all times for employee use.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The cold holding prep table in the truck is not functioning. The employees had the TCS food in a cooler on top of ice. The food was observed to be out of cold holding temperature. Cut tomatoes were probed to be at 68F, pico was probed to be at 69F, and lettuce was probed to be at 69F. CORRECTED- The operator created a suitable ice bath for the items in the top of the prep cooler and continuously stirred the items. The temperature is continuing to drop at this time. A follow up will be conduced tomorrow, 4/6/2025, to ensure that they have facility has proper cold holding. When doing an ice bath, it is important to submerge the bottom of the pans in both water and ice to allow the pans to be in an ice bath. This allows the temperature to reach the food in the pan.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The cold holding prep table in the truck is not functioning properly. The facility is using an ice bath to cold holding prep table. They are operating again tomorrow, 4/6/2025 and have someone coming to fix the cold holding prep table today. Ensure that this is repaired to allow for proper cold holding without the use of an ice bath.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
The facility is using trash bags as liners for their chip containers and could not provide if they are food grade or not. Food should be stored in a container that is smooth and easily cleanable. Cease using trash bags and use the containers to store the chips. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The facility has a Quaternary ammonium sanitizer spray bottle that is being used for sanitizer and they do not have test strips for the sanitizer. The facility is operating again tomorrow and should have test strips for QUAT. A follow up will be conducted tomorrow, 4/6/2025, to ensure that they have obtained test strips for their sanitizer. Ensure that there is always a test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration of the sanitizer.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
One employee on the truck that was stated to be there for on and off a year is observed to not have their food handlers certificate. Ensure that all employees who have been employed for greater than 30 days have their food handler certificate. These certificates should be printed and accessible to view to the inspector. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: There was not a CFPM in the mobile. The only employees were food handlers. Ensure that there is always a person in charge who is a CFPM. 

(A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: The food employee was observed to touch nonfood contact surfaces with his gloves and continue to prepare food with the same gloves. Ensure that when gloves become contaminated that we immediately wash our hands and then put on new gloves to avoid contamination to the food. CORRECTED- The employee was corrected by the person in charge and the employee was educated on handwashing. 

 (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: There were not any paper towels available at the handwashing sink to allow for proper handwashing with the use of a barrier. CORRECTED- There were napkins that were placed at the handwashing sink to be able to use a barrier and the staff was educated. 

Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: There was not any sanitizer made and available for use while the mobile was in operation. CORRECTED- The PIC was educated and made a sanitizer bucket using bleach. The sanitizer bucket tested to be at 100ppm. Ensure that there is always sanitizer available to ensure food contact surfaces are being properly cleaned. 

 (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The facility is using campfire burners in their steam table to ensure that the steam table is staying at 135F and above. This is not a proper method of hot holding. The food in the steam table was only being held between 96F and 105F. CORRECTED- The burners were relit and the food reached temperatures above 135F. Ensure that hot TCS food is maintained at a temperature of 135F and above. 

 (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The main prep cooler was holding TCS cold foods between 47F and 54F. CORRECTED- The food had only been in the cooler for a couple hours and was transferred to the other prep cooler. Ensure that TCS foods in a cooler are being held at 41F or below. 

 (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: The steam table is currently using campfire burners to maintain hot holding temperatures at 135F and above. These campfire burners were not lit during the inspection and the food was being held at between 96F and 105F. This steam table needs to be able to hold temperature without the use of campfire burners and needs to be repaired. A follow up will take place on 10/7/2024 to make sure that this steam table is properly hot holding foods at 135F and above. 

The main prep cooler was holding cold TCS food at between 47F and 54F. The proper range for cold holding for TCS food is 41F or below. The food was transferred to another cooler, but the prep cooler needs to be repaired to make sure that it can properly hold foods at 41F and below. A follow up will take place on 10/7/2024 to check on the repair and ensure that the cooler is properly holding food at 41F or below. 

EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: There were single service to-go containers that were being stored in their package on the floor of the mobile. Ensure that all single service articles and utensils are stored at least 6 inches off of the ground to protect them from contamination. 

 (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: The facility did not have any test strips available to test the bleach sanitizer. The facility was given some for the next two days while they are in operation, but there needs to be test strips available on the mobile at all times. A follow up will take place on 10/7/2024 to ensure that the mobile has obtained their own Chlorine test strips. 

 A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.
